stories.title: Russia’s Alexandrova, Medvedev advance to second round of US Open
stories.summary: NEW YORK, August 31. Tennis players from Russia, Ekaterina Alexandrova and Daniil Medvedev, have advanced to the second round of the US Open in New York. Russia’s No. 1 Medvedev (seeded 7th) defeated Hugo Gaston of France 6:4, 6:2, 6:4. Meanwhile, Ekaterina Alexandrova (seeded 18th) defeated McCartney Kessler of the United States 6:2, 6:2. Kessler was not seeded. The 2026 US Open is played on outdoor hard courts at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in New York between August 30 and September 13. The tournament will award $90 million in prize money. Spain’s Carlos Alcaraz is the tournament’s reigning champion. Russian tennis players are participating in international tournaments under a neutral status, and the US Open is no exception.

stories.title: NCT to mark 10th anniv. with fountain show, fashion exhibit in Seoul
stories.summary: K-pop boy group NCT will mark its 10th anniversary with a month-long festival across Seoul, including a musical fountain show and an exhibition of stage costumes, its agency. SM Entertainment said Monday. The events will bring NCT's music, symbolic installations and the lime-green color symbolizing the group to locations around the South Korean capital. Banpo Han River Park's Moonlight Rainbow Fountain will host water shows from Tuesday to Saturday, choreographed to the hit songs by NCT's various units: NCT 127, NCT Dream, WayV, NCT Wish and NCT U. Stage costumes worn by the group will be displayed from Friday to Sunday near Lotte World Tower, as part of the 2027 Spring/Summer Seoul Fashion Week program. The final day will also feature a fashion show combining NCT's music and costumes, alongside a flea market offering stage outfits and personal items belonging to the members. Other festival attractions will include giant art balloons, nighttime lighting events and exhibitions, SM said. The 23-member multinational boy group debuted in April 2016 and primarily operates through its units rather than performing as a full group.
